title: The Taxidermist's Daughter - review
transcript: the opening of this year's chichester festival theatre season could not be more dramatic i rarely felt such goosebumps in a theater as when the lights went up on the taxidermist daughter and after an initial jump at the loud discordant sound and disturbing lighting i then heard a chilling recitation of who killed robin and saw terrified churchgoers scatter when confronted by hanging dead crows this play has chichester running in its veins it's written by chichester resident kate moss who's such a festival theater devotee that she wrote chichester festival theater at 50. now the taxidermist daughter is set in nearby fishborne i don't know how much of the credit goes to kate moss and how much to director rosheen mcbrin but this is a play designed for the festival theatre space and the production works perfectly there but it's not all about the production superb as it is at the core there's a gothic horror story a what a mystery woman is out for revenge for a crime that is unnamed for much of the play unfortunately the script doesn't quite live up to the production but it has plenty of good moments even though it doesn't really grip well that's the one minute review keep watching for more about this gothic horror story that opened chitchat festival theater's 2022 season the main character connie gifford can't remember a traumatic event from years ago in her childhood daisy prosper plays the young woman who has a sweet disposition and a vulnerability and who's trying to continue her drunken father's tottering taxidermy business and the details about how to stuff dead birds put you on edge straight away she's troubled by events from the past and the present we eventually learned that a group of leading men from the community committed crimes and because of their position in society and because the crimes were against women they've got away with it as the play says the men charged to protect us are the ones we must fear the most the message is perennial inevitably we will think that not enough has changed 100 years on when powerful men like jimmy savile and jeffrey epstein get away with crimes against women and girls for years and for audiences of revenge fiction taking the law into one's own hands is a cathartic response to the failures of the system the taxidermist daughter is not as spooky as the woman in black nor as bloody and granginal as the lieutenant of inishmore but it does a decent job in both those genre in this respect it's helped by sinead diskin's frightening music and sound and the stark flashing lightning by premar mahetta unlike her novel and which is based the set for kate moss's play doesn't have the wonderful descriptive detail of nature instead paul will's design keeps the stage bare sinister projections in gothic black and white proliferate on the back wall the floor and on hanging screens and these are often in the form of extraordinary videos by anja goulding which shows fragments of faces dark foliage water oh yes water well i've seen a lot of water on this chichester stage over the years but this projection of splashing water onto the floor was as convincing as any real water that i've seen and water is significant because fishborn is marshland and it's 1912 the year of the great flood so the action takes place as the deluge begins in fact you could say that the mystery woman is washing out evil from the community the production uses every square inch of the stage there are entrances from all directions and pieces of set often stuffed birds and display cabinets rise from a multitude of holes in the floor it does what theater does best it inspires the imagination in fact the scariest moment is probably when we finally see the crime and that's because we don't actually see it but i've given all the information we need to imagine it and that's unlike the the moments when we witness uh what happens to the victims of the mystery woman which are shown sometimes in quite grisly detail many of the characters are sketched rather than detailed portraits pearl chandra is the mystery murderer is passionate and energetic without going over the top and forbes messenger as well as connie's father crowley gifford a man plagued with guilt about what happened in his past and who is now barely holding himself together and we also meet a nice man harry a gentle young artist played by taheen modak in the end it's an enjoyable gothic horror story in a glorious production and i give the taxidermist daughter three stars i hope you enjoyed this review and if instagram and facebook thank you for watching you
